issued_at: 05:00 pm, 02 September 2026 (Valid for broadcast until the next advisory to be issued at 11:00 PM today) PILANDOK MAINTAINS ITS STRENGTH AS IT MOVES WEST NORTHWESTWARD OVER THE PHILIPPINE SEA. HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS Heavy Rainfall Outlook Refer to Weather Advisory No. 44 issued at 5:00 PM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to the Southwest Monsoon. Severe Winds The Southwest Monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds): Today until Friday (04 September): Most of Luzon and Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental. HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS A Gale Warning is in effect over the northern and western seaboards of Northern Luzon. For more details, refer to Gale Warning No. 4 issued at 5:00 PM today. 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook Up to very rough seas over the following coastal waters: Up to 5.0 m: The seaboard of Batanes; the northern and western seaboards of Babuyan Islands. Up to 4.5 m: The seaboards of Ilocos Norte and northern Ilocos Sur. Sea travel is risky for all types or tonnage of vessels. All mariners must remain in port or, if underway, seek shelter or safe harbor as soon as possible until winds and waves subside. Up to rough seas over the following coastal waters: Up to 4.0 m: The seaboard of northern La Union; the western seaboard of Pangasinan. Up to 3.5 m: The seaboard of Zambales; the western seaboard of Bataan. Up to 3.0 m: The seaboard of Lubang Islands; the northern and western seaboards of Calamian Islands and Kalayaan Islands; the southern seaboard of Bataan; the western seaboards of Cavite, Batangas, and northern Occidental Mindoro; the remaining seaboard of Babuyan Islands. Mariners of small seacrafts, including all types of motorbancas, are advised not to venture out to sea under these conditions, especially if inexperienced or operating ill-equipped vessels. Up to moderate seas over the following coastal waters: Up to 2.5 m: The seaboards of Isabela and southern Surigao del Sur; the remaining western seaboard of Palawan; the eastern seaboard of Davao Oriental; the remaining seaboards of La Union, Pangasinan, and Kalayaan Islands; the northern seaboard of mainland Cagayan; the remaining western seaboard of Occidental Mindoro. Up to 2.0 m: The seaboards of northern Aurora, Romblon, Cuyo Islands, Cagayancillo Islands, Antique, and Davao Occidental; the southern seaboards of Quezon, Marinduque, Iloilo, and Guimaras; the eastern and southern seaboards of Oriental Mindoro; the western seaboard of southern Negros Occidental; the remaining seaboards of mainland Cagayan, northern Palawan, Occidental Mindoro, Surigao del Sur, and Davao Oriental. Mariners of motorbancas and similarly sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions. Other coastal waters have forecast wave heights of less than 2.0 m. TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK It must be emphasized that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still be experienced in localities outside the landfall point and the forecast confidence cone. Refer to “Other Hazards affecting Land Areas” for more details. Furthermore, the track may still shift within the limit of the forecast confidence cone. PILANDOK is forecast to remain as a tropical storm as it moves northwestward throughout the forecast period and will remain far from the Philippine landmass. This tropical cyclone is forecast to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) tomorrow (03 September) early morning. Location of Eye/center The center of Tropical Storm PILANDOK was estimated based on all available data at 1,085 km East Northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon (23.3 °N, 132.0 °E ) Movement Moving Westward Strength Maximum sustained winds of 65 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 80 km/h Forecast Position Sep 03, 2026 02:00 AM - 1,020 km East Northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon Sep 03, 2026 02:00 PM - 1,020 km Northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon (OUTSIDE PAR) Sep 04, 2026 02:00 AM - 1,070 km Northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon (OUTSIDE PAR) Wind Signal No Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. Persons living in areas identified to be highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards are advised to follow evacuation and other instructions from local officials. For heavy rainfall warnings, thunderstorm/rainfall advisories, and other severe weather information specific to your area, please monitor products issued by your local PAGASA Regional Services Division.
